rfm_tuples.R: For the year ended December 31, 2024, we shipped more than 120,000 pumps worldwide. Sales were $940.2 million, which included $267.5 million of sales outside the United States. For the year ended December 31, 2024, we recognized $30.2 million in net revenue from pump sales as the result of the conclusion of our Tandem Choice program ... For the year ended December 31, 2023, sales were $747.7 million ... and deferral of $25.1 million of pump sales as a result of Tandem Choice.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A: parse pump-shipment + ASP claim against US pump sales table. Mode B: strip the Tandem Choice accounting noise (one-time $30.2M recognition in 2024 + $25.1M deferral in 2023) and recompute underlying growth — the FY24 vs FY23 reported delta is exaggerated by $55.3M of accounting reversal.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Reported revenue growth: $747.7M -> $940.2M = +25.7%. Adjusted (removing Tandem Choice noise): ($940.2M - $30.2M) / ($747.7M + $25.1M) = $910.0M / $772.8M = +17.8%. US pump shipments: ~81K units (+10% YoY). OUS pump shipments: ~40K units (+30% YoY). Pump sales US: $328.6M / 81K units = ~$4,058 ASP; OUS: $105.5M / 40K units = ~$2,638 ASP — OUS ASP is 35% below US, and skew to OUS (which grew 30% vs US 10%) is a future margin headwind that the 10-K narrative obscures behind the +25.7% headline.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Both numbers are disclosed honestly (Tandem Choice is itemized), but the way they are stitched together in MD&A — 'sales were $940.2 million' as the lead — overstates true underlying momentum by ~8 points. Mode B catch: the favorable mix shift toward OUS materially compresses incremental ASP, but mgmt frames OUS as pure tailwind. This is the kind of pump-shipment-vs-ASP divergence that matters for a diabetes-pump company.

rfm_tuples.R: In February 2024, we expanded our pump portfolio with the United States launch of Tandem Mobi ... Beginning in early 2024, we scaled the commercial release of Tandem Mobi in the United States, first offering CGM integration with the Dexcom G6 sensor beginning in February followed by the Dexcom G7 beginning in June. ... we continued to scale the launch of Tandem Mobi.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A: did the 10-K disclose a specific Mobi unit count or Mobi-attributed revenue? Mode B: Mobi launched 14 months pre-cutoff in the US — by now 'continued to scale' should translate into a hard number. Silence on the unit number is the signal.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Search of 10-K finds 43 mentions of 'Mobi' but ZERO disclosed unit count or revenue dollar specific to Mobi. The 10-K aggregates Mobi into total US pump shipments (~81K) without breaking out Mobi vs t:slim X2 split. No OUS Mobi launch timeline given. The Capped Call disclosure tells us mgmt expects Mobi to drive future growth (they raised $316M of 2029 Notes in March 2024 specifically against Mobi rollout) but the 10-K refuses to give a Mobi-specific KPI 12 months post-launch.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode B finding: a successful product launch produces a hero metric the company races to disclose ('we sold X Mobi units, Y% of new starts'). TNDM has had Mobi commercially available for a full year and refuses to disclose unit mix. The most likely explanation is that Mobi cannibalized t:slim X2 rather than expanded the market — which would explain why total US pump shipments grew only 10% despite a major platform launch. This is a classic backlog-of-silence signal.

rfm_tuples.R: The Dexcom G7 sensor is the fourth generation of Dexcom's CGM that we have integrated with our pump technology since 2015. We began offering our t:slim X2 pump integrated with the Dexcom G7 sensor in the United States in December 2023 and outside the United States in January 2024. In addition, in January 2024 we announced that our t:slim X2 insulin pump with Control-IQ technology is the first AID system to integrate with the Abbott FreeStyle Libre 2 Plus sensor.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A: did Dexcom integration go GA on Mobi? Mode B: Dexcom (DXCM) is also Insulet's (PODD) CGM supplier — the Dexcom dependency is not exclusive and the 10-K explicitly says agreements are terminable on short notice.
rfm_tuples.M_value: 10-K confirms Mobi was launched with G6 in Feb 2024 and G7 in June 2024 — a 4-month gap between Mobi commercial release and G7 integration is a soft-launch admission (most type-1 adopters in 2024 prefer G7). The Abbott Libre 2 Plus integration is on t:slim X2 only — not Mobi. So Mobi's CGM compatibility lagged the t:slim X2 by ~6 months and Mobi+Libre is not yet shipping. 10-K language: agreements with Dexcom 'may be subject to termination, with or without cause, on relatively short notice.'
rfm_tuples.interpretation: The CGM-integration narrative is partially incomplete: Mobi launched with the older G6 and the Libre 2 Plus integration is restricted to t:slim X2. The pump+CGM stack is a key competitive feature for switching customers, so Mobi's launch with stale CGM integration is a soft-launch tell. Not fraud, but the 'continued to scale Tandem Mobi' framing obscures the staggered CGM ramp.

rfm_tuples.R: We compete in markets worldwide with companies that manufacture insulin delivery devices, primarily Insulet, Medtronic, Ypsomed and Beta Bionics. ... in 2023 and 2024, ongoing adoption of the GLP-1 class of drugs in diabetes and news surrounding the expansion of use of GLP-1 drugs in obesity likely had a negative impact on the insulin therapy market.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A: Insulet Omnipod 5 is the direct head-to-head with Mobi. Mode B: does the 10-K name Omnipod 5 specifically, or hide behind generic 'Insulet'?
rfm_tuples.M_value: 10-K names competitors generically ('Insulet, Medtronic, Ypsomed and Beta Bionics') without naming Omnipod 5 or its specific share dynamics. By Feb 2025 Insulet had publicly disclosed Omnipod 5 outsold Mobi by a wide margin in the on-body pump segment, but TNDM's 10-K does not engage that comp directly. GLP-1 headwind is acknowledged but the magnitude is described as 'likely had a negative impact' — vague. No quantification of patient attrition to GLP-1.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Competitive framing is generic. The single most important fact — that Omnipod 5 was already winning the patch-pump comparison vs Mobi when Mobi finally launched in 2024 — is sidestepped. GLP-1 headwind is acknowledged in principle but with no quantitative measure of attrition. Mode B catch: an honest framing would name Omnipod 5 directly since Mobi was explicitly positioned to compete against it.

rfm_tuples.R: Our technology solutions are now available in the following 25 countries ... Our pump shipments outside the United States increased by 30% to nearly 40,000 pumps ... Activities outside the United States accounted for approximately 28% of our total sales during 2024.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A: international expansion claim is verifiable. Mode B: 30% OUS pump growth is the bright spot of the entire 10-K — but OUS ASP is ~$2,638 vs US ~$4,058 (35% lower) AND 96% of OUS sales are through distributors (vs 61% in US) which means margin is materially worse than reported total gross margin suggests. Is Mobi launched OUS? Filing is silent.
rfm_tuples.M_source: self_text + Mode B ASP / channel deconstruction
rfm_tuples.M_value: OUS pump revenue $105.5M / ~40K units = $2,638 ASP. US pump revenue $328.6M / ~81K units = $4,058 ASP. Distributor channel is 96% of OUS sales (10-K Note 12). Implication: if 2025 growth shifts further OUS (per the 30% vs 10% growth differential), blended ASP must decline. No Mobi OUS launch date disclosed. The 10-K does not break out which of the 25 countries are accepting Mobi vs t:slim X2-only.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: International growth is the most-celebrated narrative thread in MD&A, but Mode B math shows that growth is mathematically compressing blended ASP and gross margin. Combined with no Mobi-OUS launch date, this looks like the international 'bright spot' is partially a price-cut-driven volume push through distributors. Not a lie, but the optimistic framing fails the Mode B sanity check.

rfm_tuples.R: At December 31, 2024, we had $438.3 million in cash and cash equivalents and short-term investments. We believe that our cash and cash equivalents, short-term investments, and future cash flows from operations will be sufficient to fund our ongoing core business activities for at least the next 12 months. ... In March 2024, we completed the offering of $316.3 million aggregate principal amount of 1.50% Convertible Senior Notes due 2029 ... we used the proceeds from the offering of the 2029 Notes to repurchase approximately $246.7 million aggregate principal amount of the 2025 Notes ... as of December 31, 2024, we had approximately $40.8 million aggregate principal amount of the 2025 Notes outstanding.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A: going_concern check (none). Mode B: capital actions sequence — they pre-emptively termed-out the 2025 maturity in March 2024 (12 months before due date), an actual GOOD disclosure-quality signal. Compare to WOLF which let the 2026 maturity sit inside the going-concern window.
rfm_tuples.M_value: 10-K signal: NO_GOING_CONCERN, n_matches=0. $438.3M cash + STI vs $40.8M remaining 2025 Notes (May 2025 maturity, 5 months pre-cutoff) and $316.3M 2029 Notes. Net cash position. OCF positive $24.2M in FY24 (vs -$31.8M in 2023 — material improvement). The 2025-Note residual is fully covered 10x by cash. Capped Call Transactions purchased to limit dilution. AMF contingent payments of CHF 40M (Jan 2025) + CHF 28M (Oct 2025) total ~$76M USD also fully covered.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Capital structure is clean. They termed out the 2025 Note 12 months before maturity in a way that left the residual easily covered. OCF inflected from -$31.8M to +$24.2M YoY. This is the single best honesty signal in the filing — they did not lean on optimistic liquidity claims, and the actions match the words.

rfm_tuples.R: (b) Securities Trading Plans of Directors and Executive Officers. None. ... Stock repurchases and retirement of shares (1,107) (1) (29,999) (30,000) [FY24 stockholders-equity statement showing $30M repurchase].
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A: 10b5-1 plan disclosure absence. Mode B: $30M of share repurchases were executed during FY24 (the period of the Mobi launch and stock recovery); how does this compare to the Q1 2024 $316.3M debt raise?

The $316.3M 2029 Note raise in March 2024 — when stock was ~$30-40 — was used to retire the lower-coupon $246.7M of 2025 Notes (kept the 1.50% rate but extended maturity by 4 years). rfm_tuples.R: Our development efforts also include Sigi, our ergonomic and rechargeable patch pump, in addition to extended wear infusion technology and algorithm advancement in pursuit of offering fully closed loop technology. ... AMF Medical is the original developer of the Sigi Patch Pump, which continued to be under development and was not yet commercially available as of December 31, 2024 ... In January 2025, the Company entered into a revised agreement that removed contingent liabilities previously outlined in the Original Transaction. The Company agreed to pay CHF 40 million in January 2025 and a final payment of CHF 28 million in October 2025.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A: Sigi commercialization claim status. Mode B: AMF was acquired in January 2023 ($24.7M cash + IPR&D charges of $78.75M booked at acquisition). Two years later Sigi is still not commercially available, and the company is paying $76M (CHF 68M) of additional cash to restructure the deal — restructuring contingent earn-outs into FIXED cash payments is usually a sign that milestones were missed.
rfm_tuples.M_value: AMF acquired Jan 2023; 24 months later, Sigi still not commercially available. The January 2025 deal amendment converted variable contingent milestones into fixed CHF 68M payments (CHF 40M paid Jan 2025 + CHF 28M Oct 2025). The original deal structure made payments contingent on regulatory/commercial milestones; converting to fixed payments suggests TNDM is paying to avoid losing the asset / paying to settle disputes. The 2023 IPR&D write-up of $78.75M (almost 3x the cash purchase price) is now looking aggressively valued.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode B catch: Sigi was the second on-body-pump shot (Mobi being the first). After two years no commercial product, and the company just paid $76M of new cash to restructure the original contingent earn-out — the exact opposite of how an acquirer behaves when an asset is performing. The 10-K narrative continues to describe Sigi as 'under development' without timeline. Combined with the Mobi unit-count silence (C2), the on-body-pump strategy looks materially behind plan.

rfm_tuples.R: Operating loss $(99,127) [FY24] $(233,230) [FY23] $(92,848) [FY22] ... For the Quarter Ended December 31, 2024: Sales $282,648 ... Gross profit $157,455 ... Operating loss $(581) ... Net income $755 ... [vs Q4 2023: Sales $196,796 / Operating loss $(35,060) / Net loss $(30,002)]. ... net revenue of $30.2 million ... as a result of the Tandem Choice program.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A: Q4 2024 'inflection to operating profitability' is the headline number that supports the $22.70 cutoff-date price. Mode B: strip the $30.2M Tandem Choice non-recurring revenue and recompute Q4 GAAP operating income.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Reported Q4 2024 operating loss = $(0.6)M. Tandem Choice contributed $30.2M of revenue at near-100% gross margin (it's pure deferred-revenue recognition). Removing Tandem Choice: Q4 sales = $282.6M - $30.2M = $252.4M; gross profit = $157.5M - ~$30M = ~$127.5M; operating loss = ~$(30.6)M. The 'inflection' is entirely an accounting artifact — without Tandem Choice, Q4 2024 underlying operating loss is roughly flat with Q4 2023 ($(30.0)M reported net loss). FY24 reported operating loss $(99.1)M; ex-Tandem Choice ~$(129)M.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode B finding — this is the most important catch in the filing. The optical Q4 2024 'breakeven' that the investment narrative leans on is constructed entirely from $30.2M of one-time Tandem Choice revenue recognition (which has no Q1 2025 echo — the program ended Dec 31 2024). The next quarterly print (Q1 2025) will lose this tailwind AND face the seasonality drag (first quarter is always seasonally weakest per the 10-K). The framework's Mode B claim-evolution check predicts disappointment when ex-Tandem-Choice comparables get reported. The filing IS technically honest — Tandem Choice is itemized — but a casual MD&A reader will internalize 'company turned profitable' which is not the steady-state truth.

summary: TNDM FY24 10-K is a MIDDLE-OF-THE-ROAD disclosure: capital structure (C6), auditor (C7), insider behavior (C8), and customer concentration are textbook honest, BUT three Mode B catches reveal optimistic framing. Mode B finding #1 (C10, strongest): the headline Q4 2024 'inflection to operating profitability' ($-0.6M op loss vs $-35M YoY) is constructed entirely from $30.2M of one-time Tandem Choice revenue recognition that won't repeat in Q1 2025 — ex-Tandem Choice, Q4 2024 operating loss is approximately $-30M, roughly flat YoY. Mode B finding #2 (C2): Mobi launched US Feb 2024 yet the 10-K refuses to disclose Mobi-specific units 12 months in; total US pump shipments grew only 10% despite a major platform launch, implying significant cannibalization of t:slim X2. Mode B finding #3 (C9): the AMF/Sigi acquisition — second on-body-pump bet — has missed timelines, with January 2025 deal restructuring converting contingent earn-outs to CHF 68M of fixed cash, a tell that milestones were missed. Combined with OUS ASP compression (C5), generic competitive framing that avoids Omnipod 5 head-to-head (C4), and acknowledged GLP-1 headwind without quantification, the filing is honest-by-itemization but optimistic-by-framing. The -34% forward return is consistent with the framework correctly flagging this as a moderate-quality disclosure that will disappoint when Q1 2025 prints without the Tandem Choice tailwind. Not a 'liar' in the WOLF sense (no going-concern reversal, no auditor risk, no insider distribution) — more a 'putting lipstick on a transition-year quarter' setup that the lying-detector catches via Mode B accounting-quality decomposition.
